data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The dominant night-time UHI mechanism is direct anthropogenic heat emissions, and the UHI intensity scales proportionally with city size, population density, and energy consumption.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a city is completely powered by non-emissive renewable energy and lacks industrial heat sources, the anthropogenic contribution approaches zero.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If rural areas have intense nighttime agricultural or industrial activities emitting comparable heat, the urban-rural differential is minimized.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Cities continuously emit heat from human activities\u2014combustion engines, HVAC systems, industrial processes, and human metabolism. On clear, calm nights when natural atmospheric mixing is minimal, this anthropogenic heat is trapped near the surface, directly elevating urban air temperatures above the rural background. The cross-city variation is best explained by the magnitude of these emissions: larger cities with higher population density and greater energy consumption release more heat, resulting in a more pronounced night-time UHI.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
